notes: NCBI StatPearls Laboratory Evaluation of Immune Hemolytic Anemias was reread for PCH as a cold-reactive IgG biphasic hemolysin diagnosed by Donath-Landsteiner testing and commonly showing C3 on DAT.
PMC practical review of the Donath-Landsteiner test was reread for complement fixation at low temperature and hemolysis after rewarming.
PubMed literature was reread for the classic acute childhood/postinfectious phenotype and anti-P IgG specificity, while noting rare non-IgG/non-P exceptions.
The official USMLE 2026 Blood & Lymphoreticular domain was verified for hemolytic and immune-mediated blood disorders.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.classic_antibody: The classic Donath-Landsteiner antibody is a biphasic IgG autoantibody, usually anti-P.
claim_audit.temperature_mechanism: It binds RBC antigen and fixes complement in cooler blood; on rewarming, antibody can dissociate while complement activation proceeds, causing intravascular hemolysis.
claim_audit.dat_pattern: Because IgG may detach, DAT often detects complement/C3 without detectable IgG.
claim_audit.clinical_pattern: Modern PCH most commonly presents as an acute, often self-limited postinfectious hemolytic anemia in young children.
claim_audit.cold_agglutinin_distractor: Cold agglutinin disease is usually IgM, often anti-I, and is mechanistically distinct from the Donath-Landsteiner biphasic IgG hemolysin.
claim_audit.warm_aiha_distractor: Warm AIHA is predominantly IgG-mediated Fc-dependent extravascular splenic hemolysis.
claim_audit.g6pd_distractor: G6PD deficiency produces oxidant-mediated hemoglobin injury rather than immune complement fixation.
claim_audit.pnh_distractor: PNH is an acquired clonal PIGA/GPI-anchor defect with loss of CD55/CD59 rather than a transient autoantibody.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Acute hemoglobinuric intravascular hemolysis after infection in a child plus C3-only DAT and positive Donath-Landsteiner testing defines PCH. The mechanistic answer is a cold-binding biphasic IgG, classically anti-P, that fixes complement in the cold and lyses RBCs on warming.
adversarial_second_pass.anti_p_precision: Anti-P is classic, not universal; rare Donath-Landsteiner antibodies with alternative specificity exist. The option and rationale explicitly use the classic mechanism in a textbook phenotype and do not claim every PCH case must be anti-P.
adversarial_second_pass.immunoglobulin_precision: Rare IgM or IgA Donath-Landsteiner antibodies have been reported. The item asks for the mechanism best explaining a classic pediatric PCH presentation; classic IgG remains uniquely appropriate.
adversarial_second_pass.cold_agglutinin_challenge: Both disorders can be complement-positive and cold-associated. The positive Donath-Landsteiner test distinguishes PCH from cold agglutinin disease, and the immunoglobulin/thermal behavior differs.
adversarial_second_pass.dat_challenge: A C3-positive/IgG-negative DAT is not alone pathognomonic and may occur in other complement-mediated AIHA; the D-L test provides specificity.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All options are authentic hemolysis mechanisms and similarly detailed; the correct answer is not simply the syndrome name.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No cold-thermal-amplitude cutoff, antibody titer, complement level or hemoglobin threshold is required.
